text: The report works now, but that's not the same as the problem being closed. Without a written record, the next time someone asks if this has happened before, the answer depends entirely on whether you personally remember it, six months from now.

A useful root-cause document has four sections. Problem, stated the way it was originally reported. Root cause, stated precisely. Fix, exactly what changed. And Prevention, a specific step, not general advice.

The root cause, written precisely: the headline card was bound to Total Sales All Regions instead of the plain Total Sales. ALL of TerritoryDim ignores the region filter on purpose, correct for a benchmark, wrong for this specific card. With no region selected, both measures matched, which is exactly why it wasn't caught at build time.

Here's the difference that matters. Double-check your measures before publishing sounds responsible but gives nobody anything concrete to actually do. Any new ALL-based measure goes into a Benchmarks display folder, named so the override is explicit, is a rule someone can actually follow and a reviewer can actually check.

Keep this document next to the project, not buried in an email thread, so the next person debugging a similar mismatch finds it in under a minute. Next lesson: presenting these same findings to two very different audiences.
